workflow: Module initialization performs a compatibility probe that creates temporary records with separately allocated text fields.
Cleanup removes the probe records through a platform-dependent bulk cleanup routine.
On one implementation, that routine releases the records but leaves some embedded text allocations unreclaimed.
Leak detection at process exit reports the retained allocations as a memory leak instead of clean initialization.
summary: Platform-dependent cleanup leaks nested probe allocations
decision_reason: No existing cluster is materially identical: the failure depends on an external cleanup routine releasing container records without reclaiming their separately allocated nested fields, rather than caller-owned cleanup being omitted, ownership being reversed, or teardown ordering retaining state.
